stem: Which staffing principle is most appropriate for critically ill or injured adult clients?

options.A: Base each shift's assignments on current patient-generated nursing workload and nurse competency; staffing plans should anticipate that critically ill or injured patients generally require about one nurse for two patients.
options.B: Use the same routine patient load as a general medical-surgical unit because critical-care acuity does not materially affect staffing needs.
options.C: Assign every critically ill client permanently one-to-one regardless of current needs, therapies, workload, or nurse competency.
options.D: Use a fixed nurse-to-patient ratio as the sole assignment rule without reassessing current workload, patient needs, or nurse competency.

rationale: AACN's 2024 Standards for Appropriate Staffing in Adult Critical Care state that, for every shift, patient assignments should be based on an accurate assessment of the current nursing workload generated by each patient's needs and should align nurse competency with patient characteristics. AACN also states that organizational staffing plans should anticipate that critically ill or injured patients generally require a ratio of one nurse to two patients. Therefore A is correct. B ignores the higher and changing workload of critical care, C incorrectly makes 1:1 staffing universal and permanent, and D treats a ratio as sufficient without the workload- and competency-based reassessment AACN requires.
educational_objective: Apply critical-care staffing principles by matching current patient-generated workload and patient characteristics with nurse competency while recognizing that adult critically ill or injured patients generally require approximately one RN for two patients and may require more intensive staffing based on need.
source_document_title: AACN Standards for Appropriate Staffing in Adult Critical Care — Standards Published for Critical Care Nurse Staffing
source_version_date: Published April 23, 2024; current AACN standards page and newsroom summary live-rechecked August 16, 2026
source_locator: AACN newsroom summary > The seven standards: patient assignments for every shift are based on accurate assessment of current nursing workload generated by each patient's needs and align nurse competency with patient characteristics; organizational staffing plans anticipate that critically ill or injured patients generally require a ratio of one nurse to two patients. Current AACN Standards page confirms the 2024 adult critical-care staffing standards remain active/current.
source_claim_supported: Adult critical-care assignments should reflect current patient-generated nursing workload and nurse competency; organizational plans generally anticipate one nurse for two critically ill or injured patients rather than using a ratio as the sole inflexible assignment rule.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Management of Care, printed p.20 > Assignment, Delegation and Supervision: identify assignments based on client needs; assign appropriate tasks to personnel with competency; evaluate staff ability considering allowable duties, competency, judgment and decision-making. Establishing Priorities, printed p.21: prioritize care based on acuity.
blueprint_topic: Management of Care — staffing assignments based on client needs, acuity, workload, and nurse competency

source_original.stem: Which staffing principle is most appropriate for critically ill clients?

options.A: Match assignments to acuity, workload, and nurse competency; many critically ill clients require about one nurse for two patients.
options.B: Use the same routine patient load as a general medical-surgical unit because ICU acuity does not change staffing needs.
options.C: Assign every critically ill client permanently one-to-one regardless of condition, therapy, workload, or available support.
options.D: Use a fixed ratio alone without considering patient acuity, workload, nurse competency, or changes in clinical condition.

source_original.rationale: AACN staffing standards emphasize matching nursing assignments to current patient needs, workload, and nurse competency; critically ill patients generally require approximately one nurse for every two patients, with some requiring more intensive staffing. Option A is correct. B underestimates acuity, while C and D incorrectly make staffing an inflexible rule.
source_original.source_detail: Critical-care staffing standards: critically ill/injured patients generally require about one nurse for every two patients; assignments must reflect patient needs/acuity, workload, and nurse competency, with additional support for nurses new to a unit. AACN staffing standards published 2024-04-23 and current; live-rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN 2026 Management of Care assignment/competency check completed first. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care: prioritization, assignment/delegation, advocacy/client rights, continuity/referral, legal scope, professional limitations and emergency/quality-management activities as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: Retained the staffing construct and key A, but tightened the wording to AACN's exact certainty level: critically ill or injured adult patients generally require a 1:2 ratio, while each shift's assignment still depends on current patient-generated workload and nurse competency. Replaced vague 'many' language, made the distractors more parallel, and changed difficulty from hard to medium because the final item tests a defined staffing standard rather than complex multi-step clinical synthesis.

audit_findings.clinical_category: Adult critical-care nurse staffing and assignment
audit_findings.source_authority: Current AACN adult critical-care staffing standards; official NCSBN 2026 Test Plan for blueprint
audit_findings.currentness: AACN 2024 staffing standards remain the current adult critical-care staffing standard on AACN's 2026 standards site; live-rechecked 2026-08-16
audit_findings.exact_locator: AACN newsroom > seven staffing standards, especially current workload/competency assignment standard and general 1:2 planning standard; NCSBN printed p.20 Assignment, Delegation and Supervision
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final item uses AACN's explicit current-workload, nurse-competency, and general 1:2 planning statements. It does not assert that every ICU patient is always 1:2 or 1:1 and does not treat ratio alone as sufficient for assignment decisions.

distractor_audit.B: Incorrect because critical-care assignments must reflect patient-generated workload and needs rather than a routine med-surg load.
distractor_audit.C: Incorrect because AACN does not require universal permanent 1:1 staffing; assignment intensity depends on current need/workload.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrect because AACN requires current workload and competency assessment rather than a fixed ratio as the sole rule.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A combines the AACN workload/competency standard with the general organizational 1:2 staffing expectation without converting it into an inflexible ratio rule.
audit_findings.cueing: All options address staffing methodology and ratio use; no option is keyed by an unrelated mechanism or unsupported numeric threshold.
audit_findings.blueprint: Management of Care — Assignment, Delegation and Supervision; acuity-based prioritization.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Re-audited the AACN current standards summary, current AACN standards page, NCSBN 2026 PDF text and rendered printed p.20, all four alternatives, rationale, objective, difficulty, ambiguity, cueing, and certainty language. A remained uniquely defensible.
